newsitem.title: FRANCE: US court throws out Parretti claim over MGM.
newsitem.headline: US court throws out Parretti claim over MGM.

text.p: A U.S. court has dismissed a $3.9 billion lawsuit launched by Italian financier Giancarlo Parretti against French bank Credit Lyonnais after it foreclosed on his loan to buy Hollywood studio MGM, French officials said on Tuesday.

The court in Los Angeles "threw out Mr. Giancarlo Parretti's demands in the affair of MGM," on March 13, said state-backed holding company Consortium de Realisation, which took over the bank's bad loans including the $1.3 billion one it made to Parretti to buy Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer.
State-controlled bank Credit Lyonnais, which ran up massive losses in the early 1990s from a lending spree that went sour, was saddled with MGM when the former movie mogul defaulted on the loan.

Parretti, who lost control of the studio to his bankers in 1991, had alleged in the suit that Credit Lyonnais acted improperly in foreclosing on the loan and had conspired to take the movie studio from him.
The loan was made by the bank's former Dutch unit CLBN.
Last month, Parretti forfeited $25,000 bail after failing to return from Italy for sentencing in Delaware on a conviction of perjury and evidence tampering that carried a maximum penalty of 10 years.
Legal sources had said his failure to return to the United States meant he would lose the California lawsuit against the bank by default.

"This decision (on March 13) puts an end -- to the complete satisfaction of the Consortium de Realisation (CDR) -- to a court case involving $3.9 billion which Mr Parretti had thought it worthwhile claiming in 1994," the agency said in a statement.
"This is an important moment in the Parretti affair," a spokesman for the state holding company said later.
Parretti was indicted in Delaware in 1992 on charges he doctored documents and lied about it over his ouster from MGM by the French bank.
The Delaware case is just one of a myriad of legal cases in which Parretti is enmeshed in the United States.
Parretti's lawyer has said his client was forced to return home to Italy to face a separate probe in Italy into alleged tax fraud.

The CDR, which sold MGM last year for $1.3 billion to an acquisition team led by MGM chairman Frank Mancuso and backed by billionaire Kirk Kerkorian, said the decision was independent of other legal action under way in France and in the United States against Parretti.

Delaware and California authorities have begun extradition proceedings against Parretti but justice authorities in the United States have said they are unsure whether Italy would arrest Parretti on a U.S. warrant.
France is also seeking his extradition on a number of charges, including abuse of corporate assets.
